extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, counsel and parties in AIA trials before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (IPR, PGR, CBM, derivation)
extracted.subtask_description: Practice and procedural guidance for conducting AIA trials before the PTAB (inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review, and derivation proceedings), covering jurisdiction, filings, discovery, motions, hearings, confidentiality, and evidence rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. § 6(b) provides that the Board is to conduct derivation proceedings, inter partes reviews, and post-grant reviews. The Board will have exclusive jurisdiction within the Office over every application and patent that is involved in a derivation, IPR, PGR, or CBM proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings are not 'involved' patents and are treated separately except as ordered by the Board. Use jurisdictional rules to identify which matters the Board controls and when stays, transfers, consolidation, or termination are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Ex Parte Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All substantive communications with the Board regarding a proceeding must include all parties to the proceeding, except as otherwise authorized. 37 C.F.R. § 42.5(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: ministerial communications with support staff; conference calls/hearings where opposing counsel declines to participate; informing the Board of related Board proceedings; referencing a pending case to support a general proposition. When arranging conference calls, parties should meet and confer first and be prepared to explain the need and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arranging a Conference Call with the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board encourages the use of conference calls to raise and resolve issues in an expedited manner. Parties should meet and confer prior to requesting a call; if unsuccessful, a party may request a call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting a call be prepared to discuss why the call is needed and what materials may be needed. Notify the Board if a court reporter will be present; if so, file transcript as an exhibit within one week of receipt. The Board may permit calls even if a party refuses to participate, imposing safeguards as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to Participate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board has the discretion to permit a hearing or conference call to take place even if a party refuses to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may order safeguards (e.g., recording and entering the recording into the record) as a condition for holding the call without participation by all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for Lead and Back-up Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: A party represented by counsel must designate both a lead as well as a back-up counsel who can conduct business on behalf of the lead counsel. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead counsel is expected to participate in hearings and sign papers; back-up counsel must be able to act when lead counsel is unavailable and may conduct actions not before the Office (e.g., depositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Attorney Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney must be filed with the designation of counsel, unless the designated counsel is already counsel of record. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely filing of power of attorney along with counsel designation to avoid procedural issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Hac Vice Admission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may recognize counsel pro hac vice upon a showing of good cause, and subject to the requirement that lead counsel is a registered practitioner. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant is discretionary and considers complexity, potential amendments, competence, willingness to follow Rules of Professional Conduct, and civility. The Board may revoke pro hac vice for various reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Filing Default
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic filing is the default manner in which documents are to be filed with the Board. 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing improves efficiency and accessibility. Paper filing requires a motion explaining the need; rare exceptions include electronic system failures. Parties may request short extensions when filing problems occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must provide mandatory notices including identification of the real parties-in-interest, related matters, lead and back-up counsel, and service information. 37 C.F.R. § 42.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information changes, file a revised notice within 21 days. Failure to disclose relevant parties or related matters can affect estoppel and other outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Party-in-Interest or Privy Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must identify 'real parties-in-interest' and 'privies' to assist in identifying potential conflicts and ensuring proper application of statutory estoppel provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board applies traditional common-law principles and flexible, fact-dependent analysis (Taylor v. Sturgell). Considerations include funding, direction, and control of a petition or proceeding; control and close relationships can justify labeling a non-party. CBM proceedings have additional statutory standing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Matters Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must disclose related matters (e.g., pending district court suits, other USPTO matters) as part of mandatory notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure helps the Board manage parallel proceedings, determine stays, consolidations, or other coordination; failure to disclose may have procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Service Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must include proper identification of service information in filings as required by 37 C.F.R. § 42.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep service contacts updated and file changes promptly to ensure service and notices are effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Availability of Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board's default posture is public availability of filings unless confidential information is properly sealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to seal and protective orders govern what information may be restricted from public view; parties should prepare non-confidential redacted versions when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Information Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential information must be identified and handled according to Board rules and protective orders; confidential material should be marked appropriately and filed under seal when warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board rarely needs source code; protective orders should avoid incompatible district court terms (e.g., prosecution bars) and should be tailored to Board procedures. Use motions to seal with non-confidential descriptions of the sealed material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Seal Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Motion to Seal should provide a non-confidential description of the nature of the confidential information and reasons why it should not be public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where only some information is confidential, file both confidential and redacted non-confidential versions, clearly indicating redactions. The Board will decide whether redacted material qualifies for protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Protective orders govern the treatment and filing of confidential information and should be consistent with Board procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Practice Guide provides a Default Protective Order and guidelines. Proposed protective orders that conflict with Board procedures (e.g., regarding filings, handling confidential info) should be revised before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Information in Petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties filing petitions that include confidential information must follow procedures for sealing and redaction when submitting to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Motion to Seal procedures and provide non-confidential summaries where possible; Board will determine confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of Confidential Information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board provides mechanisms to expunge confidential information from the record when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move for expungement and justify why material should be removed. Procedures and standards are governed by the rules and Board discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation Proceedings Confidential and Procedural Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivation proceedings have particular confidentiality, estoppel, and procedural rules and may involve arbitration by parties though the Office retains authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that derivation rules were effective later than other AIA rules and that derivation proceedings differ in available remedies and interactions with other proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of Discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery will generally proceed in a sequenced fashion consistent with the Scheduling Order—e.g., patent owner may depose petitioner's declarants after institution; petitioner may depose patent owner declarants after patent owner response and motion to amend; further depositions occur after replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequencing is intended to streamline issues and focus discovery. After discovery ends parties may file motions to exclude evidence. Admissibility governed generally by the Federal Rules of Evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine Discovery (37 C.F.R. § 42.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine discovery includes production of documents and information identified in the rules, such as inconsistent statements and basic documentary evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider specifics: (a) Inconsistent statements, (b) witness expenses, (c) document translation; follow rules for timing and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may seek additional discovery beyond routine discovery upon demonstrating relevance and need; such discovery is subject to Board authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional discovery requests should be narrowly tailored; Board may permit depositions of witnesses identified in new declarations or other targeted discovery tied to specific issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelled Testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may compel testimony where appropriate under the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use motions and follow 37 C.F.R. § 42 provisions for compelled testimony; be prepared to schedule examinations and address privilege claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Initial Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board requires mandatory initial disclosures from parties as set forth in the trial rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with disclosure timelines and substance requirements to avoid discovery disputes and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Live testimony (cross-examination, redirect, compelled direct) occurs by oral examination; uncompelled direct testimony is usually presented by affidavit or declaration. 37 C.F.R. § 42.53(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Testimony Guidelines for oath, recording, objections, and limitations on coaching. The Board expects question-and-answer cross-examination; defending counsel must not coach or act as intermediary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Times and Locations for Witness Cross-Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scheduling Order will set times and locations for witness cross-examination; parties must comply with those settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should coordinate logistics early and request adjustments through the Board where necessary; the Board may allow changes for fairness or practical reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Discovery Model Order and Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix C provides a Model Order Regarding E-Discovery: streamlines ESI production to promote just, speedy, and inexpensive resolution consistent with 37 C.F.R. § 42.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key rules: generally exclude metadata; general ESI production shall not include email (email requires specific request and Board authorization); email requests must identify custodian, search terms, and timeframe; limits: five custodians per producing party and five search terms per custodian (subject to Board modification upon showing of need); cost-shifting for disproportionate requests; cooperation required on custodians/search terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony is subject to the Trial Rules and the Practice Guide; expert declarations must disclose underlying facts or data and conform to procedural requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure experts state bases for opinions, attach supporting data, and be prepared for depositions; follow rules on scope, disclosure, and admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Motions Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions practice is governed by 37 C.F.R. § 42 and the Practice Guide; prior authorization may be required for certain filings and motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet and confer before filing motions, obtain prior authorization where required, and follow page/word limits. Motions should be concise, identify relief sought, and rely on relevant authorities and facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Authorization for Certain Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain discovery requests and other requests require prior Board authorization before propounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include extensive email discovery; parties must seek Board permission and justify the scope and necessity of such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word Count and Page Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board enforces word count and page limits for filings; parties must comply unless prior authorization is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Board's word-count rules to calculate compliance; excessive filings may be rejected or require leave. The Guide includes practice updates on use of word counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony Must Disclose Underlying Facts or Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony and declarations must disclose the underlying facts or data supporting the opinions and statements made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conclusory testimony; attach exhibits, data, and references that support factual assertions and expert opinions to enable meaningful cross-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests and Data
rubrics_metrics.description: When relying on tests or data, parties must disclose methodologies, underlying data, and any assumptions supporting conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient methodological detail to allow assessment of reliability and relevance; failure to do so may lead to exclusion or reduced weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective Indicia of Nonobviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective indicia (secondary considerations) should be presented where relevant to nonobviousness analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence (e.g., commercial success, long-felt need, copying, unexpected results) with supporting data and linkages to claimed features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition Filing Date and Minimum Procedural Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition must be filed consistent with statutory time periods and be accompanied by the evidence the petitioner relies upon; minimum procedural compliance determines filing date. 35 U.S.C. §§ 135(a), 311(c); 37 C.F.R. § 42.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required parts (claims challenged, grounds, evidence, notices) are included to secure a proper filing date; failure may cause filing date vacatur or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of Proof for Statutory Institution Thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must establish that the standards for instituting the requested trial are met, taking into account any patent owner preliminary response; the Board may institute only if statutory thresholds are met (see 35 U.S.C. §§ 314, 324).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare petition to address the relevant statutory threshold (e.g., reasonable likelihood of success for IPR or the 'more likely than not' standard for some PGRs), and anticipate patent owner preliminary response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Requirements for a Petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must identify all challenged claims and the grounds and supporting evidence on a claim-by-claim basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include claim charts, reference to prior art, declarations, and exhibits; ensure claim-by-claim analysis to satisfy rule requirements and to assist Board evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered Business Method (CBM) / Technological Invention Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM proceedings have special statutory requirements; the petition must address whether the patent qualifies as a covered business method or technological invention as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CBM, the petitioner (or its real party-in-interest/privy) must meet statutory prerequisites such as having been sued or charged with infringement in certain contexts; be prepared to address the technological invention exception when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim charts should present a claim-by-claim mapping of prior art to claim limitations to support unpatentability grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, specific mappings with citations and supporting evidence; vague or conclusory charts can undermine the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will construe claims for purposes of the trial; claim construction is integral to institution and to motions to amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should present proposed constructions with supporting intrinsic/extrinsic evidence; claim construction can affect institution decisions and amendment practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Preliminary Response
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPR, PGR, and CBM, the patent owner may file a preliminary response within three months of notification of a filing date, including electing not to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-crafted preliminary response can persuade the Board not to institute; address threshold issues, standing, and sufficiency of petitioner’s evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution of Trial — Statutory Threshold Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will institute a trial only where the petitioner establishes that standards for instituting the requested trial are met, taking into account any preliminary response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board's decision must be either to institute on all claims/grounds in the petition or to deny institution entirely (post-SAS Institute). The Board provides analysis of strengths and weaknesses when instituting to guide the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in Instituting a Review (35 U.S.C. §§ 314(a), 324(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board considers statutory factors, prior art overlap, prior proceedings, and efficiency in deciding whether to institute review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include prior PTAB or court consideration of the same art, parallel petitions, prior PTO examination, and interface with district court litigation; 35 U.S.C. § 325(d) may bar institution when issues were previously addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel Petitions Challenging the Same Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple petitions challenge the same patent, the Board may determine how proceedings will proceed, including joinder, consolidation, or termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will consider efficiency and potential for inconsistent rulings; parties should flag related petitions and consider motions for joinder or consolidation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. § 325(d) — Prior Art Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 325(d) allows the Board to deny institution where the same or substantially the same prior art or arguments were previously presented to the Office and were not successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must distinguish prior proceedings or show why those earlier considerations do not negate the current petition; failure to account for prior Office consideration may lead to denial under § 325(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of Decision on Whether to Institute
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board's institution decision will set forth reasoning and generally provide analysis of strengths and weaknesses of all challenges in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institution decisions as guidance for upcoming trial; parties dissatisfied may request rehearing for overlooked or misapprehended points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will enter a Scheduling Order concurrent with the decision to institute a trial setting due dates for the proceeding to ensure completion within one year of institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling Orders set dates for discovery phases, patent owner response, motions to amend, petitioner replies, and hearing. Sample scheduling orders are in Appendix A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Conference Call (One Month After Institution, If Requested)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may request an initial conference call about one month after institution to discuss intended motions and adjustments to the Scheduling Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this call to flag timing, discovery sequencing, and any special issues; request promptly and meet-and-confer beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Response (Post-Institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: After institution, the patent owner may file a response and/or motion to amend claims by dates set in the Scheduling Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should address substantive defenses, procedural issues, and include motions to amend if desired; prepare for subsequent petitioner oppositions and discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to Amend — General Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to amend are governed by specific practice rules for IPR, PGR, and CBM; parties should follow motion timing, content, and evidentiary standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board expects motions to amend to comply with contents requirements, include proposed claims and show patentability, and be filed by scheduled dates. The Guide provides practice tips and a sample framework for motions to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Amend — Due Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to amend must be filed by the due date set in the Scheduling Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late motions require Board leave and are disfavored; calendar carefully to meet Scheduling Order deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to Amend — Evidentiary Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to amend are subject to evidentiary standards requiring sufficient supporting evidence to show proposed amended claims are patentable over the prior art of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide declarations, tests, and factual support tying proposed claim features to patentability; be prepared for oppositions and cross-examination of declarants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Motion to Amend
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend should include the proposed substitute claims, claim support in the specification, arguments and evidence of patentability, and any necessary claim construction positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate written support in the patent specification and explain how substituted claims differ from prior art; follow the procedural content requirements closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Construction in Motion to Amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim construction principles apply to motions to amend and the Board may apply constructions consistent with trial practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue constructions as needed to support patentability of amended claims, using intrinsic and extrinsic evidence; be aware of how constructions affect novelty and obviousness assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in Derivation Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment practice in derivation proceedings follows specific rules and may differ from IPR/PGR/CBM amendment practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult derivation-specific provisions for amendment content and timing; coordinate amendment strategy with derivation issues such as inventorship and priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Practice Tips on Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on amendment practice includes preparing robust support, anticipating oppositions, and timely presenting evidence to support patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overbroad or unsupported amendments; provide clear specification support and factual bases; consider strategic timing and scope of proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to a Motion to Amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner may oppose motions to amend by filing oppositions addressing adequacy of support and patentability over prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions should point to prior art, claim construction, and record deficiencies; include declarations where needed to rebut patent owner evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies and Sur-Replies
rubrics_metrics.description: The schedule permits petitioner replies to patent owner responses and oppositions to motions to amend, and patent owner sur-replies in limited circumstances; use of sur-replies may substitute for observations in some contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Scheduling Order on allowed sur-replies (e.g., in pilot programs some timelines allow six-week replies/sur-replies); do not introduce new issues or evidence beyond permitted scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Motions — Joinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions for joinder are available and governed by rule; the Board has discretion to grant joinder of additional parties or petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File joinder motions timely and show reasons for consolidation or joinder; the Board balances efficiency, prejudice, and procedural fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging Admissibility; Motions to Exclude; Motions to Strike
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file motions to exclude inadmissible evidence and motions to strike improper material; admissibility governed generally by Federal Rules of Evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File motions after discovery closes; follow evidentiary standards, cite specific grounds (e.g., hearsay, lack of foundation), and support with legal and factual argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral Hearing Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may request an oral hearing; the Board will set the hearing and address special equipment, demonstrative exhibits, and live testimony logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new evidence or arguments permitted at hearing. File demonstrative exhibits and identify special equipment or needs in advance. Live testimony must comply with testimony guidelines and time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may terminate the proceeding by filing a written agreement, unless the Board has decided the merits; if no petitioner remains the Board may terminate or proceed to final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File settlement papers promptly and note any statutory or procedural constraints; Board approval may be required in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Decision and Remands
rubrics_metrics.description: When a trial is instituted and not dismissed, the Board will issue a final written decision with respect to challenged claims. The Board may remand to the Office in appropriate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decisions are issued under statutory deadlines; consider appeals and potential remands in strategic planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with Board determinations (e.g., institution decision) may request rehearing as to points believed to be overlooked or misapprehended. See 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.71(c), (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing requests should focus on oversight or misapprehension and not merely reargue the same points; follow timing and form requirements for rehearing petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default Protective Order — Marking and Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential information shall be clearly marked 'PROTECTIVE ORDER MATERIAL.' Access is limited to enumerated categories: parties, party representatives, experts (subject to certification), in-house counsel, support personnel, and Office employees with need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support personnel may be informed rather than sign acknowledgements; other employees/consultants require motion and acknowledgement. The producing party may oppose disclosure to particular persons; the opposing party bears burden to restrict access. Use secure procedures and limit copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default Protective Order — Filing and Production Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing procedures: a party may file documents under seal with a Motion to Seal and a non-confidential description; where only some info is confidential, file confidential and redacted non-confidential versions indicating redactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents exchanged among parties must be marked and produced to maintain confidentiality. Confidential material remains under seal unless Board rules otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default Protective Order — Return/Destruction After Final Disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after final disposition (including appeals), each party receiving confidential information must return or certify destruction of all copies of the confidential information to the producing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of destroyed or returned materials and comply with timelines to avoid violations of protective order obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default Protective Order — Acknowledgment Form
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard acknowledgement form is provided for individuals to certify they have read and will abide by the Protective Order and will use confidential information only in connection with the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement includes submitting to jurisdiction of the Office and EDVA for enforcement and committing to limited use and disclosure rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Discovery — Metadata and Email Production
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless authorized, ESI production shall not include metadata; general ESI production shall not include email. Email production requires specific requests authorized by the Board and must identify custodian, search terms, and time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields indicating date/time and distribution list should generally be included. Email production is phased after initial production and is limited and targeted to specific issues to prevent overbroad discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Discovery — Custodian and Search Term Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each requesting party shall limit email production requests to five custodians per producing party and five search terms per custodian (subject to agreement or Board authorization for additional custodians/terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search terms must be narrowly tailored; conjunctive combinations count as single terms; disjunctive combinations count separately unless variants. Parties should cooperate in identifying custodians and terms; cost-shifting may apply for disproportionate requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Discovery — Privilege Protections and Inadvertent Production
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving party shall not use ESI asserted to be attorney-client privileged or work product to challenge privilege. Inadvertent production is not a waiver under Federal Rule of Evidence 502(b) if reasonable steps were taken to prevent disclosure and promptly rectified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere production of ESI in a mass production shall not itself constitute a waiver of privilege for any purpose before the Office (analogous to FRE 502(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony Guidelines — Form and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncompelled direct testimony is almost always presented by affidavit or declaration; other testimony occurs by oral examination. Testimony must be recorded and follows Federal Rules practice except Rule 103 does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections during examination must be concise and non-suggestive (e.g., 'Objection, form'); coaching and speaking objections are prohibited. Counsel may instruct a witness not to answer only to preserve privilege, enforce Board limits, or present motions. Sanctions may be imposed for impeding fair examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony Guidelines — Cross-Examination Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-examination should be a question-and-answer conversation between the examining lawyer and the witness; defending counsel must not act as intermediary or coach the witness; counsel offering the witness on direct may not confer about substance during cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel shall not initiate private conferences during pending questions except to determine whether to assert privilege. The Board may impose sanctions, including expenses and attorneys’ fees, for improper conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony Guidelines — Duration and Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless agreed or ordered otherwise, testimony is limited in duration to times set in 37 C.F.R. § 42.53(c). Testimony may be suspended if a witness or party moves to terminate or limit because of bad faith or unreasonable behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If testimony is suspended, promptly initiate a conference call with the Board for resolution; the Board may allow additional time where fairness requires.
